notes: The market-side weak signal for SI8: if adaptation lags, flood-risk communities in Wales face an insurance affordability cliff from 2039, which would directly undermine places continuing to support well-being in a changing climate. Coverage and statistics are England-heavy but the scheme is UK-wide and the mechanism applies fully to Wales. Pairs with the CCC's warning that adaptation funding falls short of the 2 degree planning commitment.
summary: The Flood Re reinsurance scheme that keeps UK flood insurance affordable is scheduled to end in 2039 on the assumption that flood risk will have fallen enough for risk-reflective pricing. Industry analysis (February 2026) doubts adaptation will move fast enough, with around 8 million properties in England alone projected at flood risk by 2050 and rising numbers of homes already hard to insure. On 1 July 2026 Flood Re and Defra announced a reform package to prepare for the 2039 exit: Flood Performance Certificates with premium discounts, an expanded Build Back Better resilience grant of up to 10,000 pounds, and a cut in contents-only premiums for Council Tax Bands A and B from 52 to 25 pounds from April 2027.
title: Flood Re ends in 2039: insurance affordability cliff if adaptation lags climate risk
